Apple___Apple_scab.cause: Fungus (Venturia inaequalis); spreads in cool, wet spring weather.
Apple___Apple_scab.symptoms: Olive-green to dark brown, velvety spots on leaves; leaves may yellow and drop early.
Apple___Apple_scab.management: Rake up and destroy fallen leaves, prune for airflow, plant resistant varieties, and apply protective fungicides in spring as advised locally.

Apple___Black_rot.cause: Fungus (Botryosphaeria obtusa); survives in dead wood, cankers and mummified fruit.
Apple___Black_rot.symptoms: 'Frog-eye' leaf spots: tan to brown centres with a purple margin.
Apple___Black_rot.management: Prune out dead wood and cankers, remove mummified fruit, and use fungicide sprays during the season if the disease is common.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.cause: Fungus (Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae); alternates between apple and juniper / red cedar.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on the upper leaf surface; small tube-like structures form underneath later.
Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.management: Plant resistant varieties, remove nearby junipers where practical, and apply fungicide from bloom to early summer if needed.

Apple___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Blueberry___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungus (Podosphaera clandestina); favoured by warm days and humid nights.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery patches on young leaves; leaves may curl or distort.
Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.management: Prune for airflow, avoid excess nitrogen, and apply sulfur or other labelled fungicides at the first signs.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.cause: Fungus (Cercospora zeae-maydis); survives on crop residue, favoured by warm, humid weather.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.symptoms: Long, narrow, rectangular grey to tan lesions bounded by leaf veins.
Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.management: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops, manage residue, and consider a foliar fungicide when disease is severe.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.cause: Fungus (Puccinia sorghi); spores blow in on the wind.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.symptoms: Small, elongated, cinnamon-brown pustules on both leaf surfaces.
Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.management: Plant resistant hybrids. Fungicide is rarely needed except on susceptible sweet corn with early, heavy infection.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.cause: Fungus (Exserohilum turcicum); survives on residue, favoured by moderate temperatures and long leaf wetness.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions, often several centimetres long.
Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.management: Use resistant hybrids, rotate crops, manage residue, and apply fungicide around tasselling if risk is high.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Grape___Black_rot.cause: Fungus (Guignardia bidwellii); survives in mummified berries and canes.
Grape___Black_rot.symptoms: Circular tan to brown leaf spots with a dark border and tiny black dots; berries shrivel into black mummies.
Grape___Black_rot.management: Remove mummies and infected canes, open the canopy for airflow, and spray fungicide from bloom until a few weeks after.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).cause: A complex of wood-infecting fungi (e.g. Phaeomoniella chlamydospora) that enter through pruning wounds.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).symptoms: 'Tiger-stripe' leaves: yellow or red-brown bands between the veins; dark spots on berries.
Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).management: No cure. Prune in dry weather, protect pruning wounds, and remove badly affected vines.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.cause: Fungus (Pseudocercospora vitis); favoured by warm, wet weather.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.symptoms: Irregular dark brown spots that can merge; affected leaves may drop early.
Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.management: Remove fallen leaves, improve airflow, and use the fungicide programme used for other grape diseases.

Grape___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).cause: Bacterium (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus) spread by the Asian citrus psyllid.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).symptoms: Blotchy, uneven yellowing that is not symmetrical across the midrib; small, lopsided, bitter fruit.
Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).management: No cure. Remove infected trees, control psyllids, use certified disease-free nursery plants, and report suspected cases where required.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacterium (Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni); spread by wind-driven rain.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, angular, water-soaked spots turning purple-brown; centres may fall out, leaving 'shot holes'.
Peach___Bacterial_spot.management: Plant resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, and apply copper sprays early in the season as advised locally.

Peach___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacteria (Xanthomonas spp.); carried on seed and spread by splashing water.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked spots that turn brown, often with a yellow halo; leaves may drop.
Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.management: Use disease-free seed and transplants, rotate crops for 2-3 years, avoid overhead watering; copper sprays can slow spread.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Potato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria solani); starts on older, lower leaves.
Potato___Early_blight.symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings (a 'target' pattern), often with a yellow halo.
Potato___Early_blight.management: Rotate crops, remove plant debris, keep plants well fed, and use labelled fungicides when disease appears.

Potato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans); spreads very fast in cool, wet weather.
Potato___Late_blight.symptoms: Pale green to dark brown, water-soaked patches; white mould on the leaf underside in humid conditions.
Potato___Late_blight.management: Act quickly: destroy infected plants, use certified seed tubers, and apply preventive fungicides when weather favours the disease.

Potato___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Raspberry___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Soybean___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.cause: Fungi (e.g. Podosphaera xanthii); favoured by dry leaves and high humidity.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.symptoms: White, powdery spots on leaves that spread and merge; leaves yellow and die.
Squash___Powdery_mildew.management: Plant resistant varieties, space plants for airflow, and apply sulfur, potassium bicarbonate or other labelled fungicides early.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.cause: Fungus (Diplocarpon earlianum); spreads by splashing water.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.symptoms: Many small purple spots that enlarge until the leaf looks scorched.
Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.management: Remove infected leaves after harvest, renovate beds, avoid overhead watering, and plant resistant varieties.

Strawberry___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.cause: Bacteria (Xanthomonas spp.); carried on seed and spread by splashing water.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves, sometimes with a yellow halo; scabby spots on fruit.
Tomato___Bacterial_spot.management: Use clean seed and transplants, rotate crops, avoid overhead watering and handling wet plants; copper sprays help only partly.

Tomato___Early_blight.cause: Fungus (Alternaria spp.); starts on older, lower leaves.
Tomato___Early_blight.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings (a 'target' pattern) and yellowing around them.
Tomato___Early_blight.management: Rotate crops, mulch, remove infected lower leaves, stake plants for airflow, and use labelled fungicides if needed.

Tomato___Late_blight.cause: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans); spreads very fast in cool, wet weather.
Tomato___Late_blight.symptoms: Large, greasy grey-green to brown blotches; white growth on the underside; firm brown rot on fruit.
Tomato___Late_blight.management: Remove and destroy infected plants promptly, keep foliage dry, use resistant varieties and preventive fungicides.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.cause: Fungus (Passalora fulva); common in greenhouses and high humidity.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.symptoms: Pale green to yellow spots on the upper surface; olive-green to brown velvety mould underneath.
Tomato___Leaf_Mold.management: Lower humidity, ventilate and space plants, plant resistant varieties, and use fungicides if needed.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.cause: Fungus (Septoria lycopersici); spreads by splashing water, starts on lower leaves.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.symptoms: Many small, round spots with dark borders and grey-tan centres, often with tiny black dots.
Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.management: Remove infected lower leaves, rotate crops, mulch, avoid overhead watering, and use labelled fungicides.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.cause: Pest (Tetranychus urticae), not a pathogen; thrives in hot, dry weather.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.symptoms: Fine yellow or white speckling, bronzing, and fine webbing on the leaf underside.
Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.management: Spray leaves with water, encourage predatory mites, use insecticidal soap or horticultural oil, and avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill natural enemies.

Tomato___Target_Spot.cause: Fungus (Corynespora cassiicola); favoured by warm, humid weather.
Tomato___Target_Spot.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings and a yellow halo; can look like early blight.
Tomato___Target_Spot.management: Improve airflow, remove lower leaves and debris, rotate crops, and use labelled fungicides.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.cause: Virus (TYLCV) spread by the whitefly Bemisia tabaci.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.symptoms: Leaves curl upward with yellow margins; plants are stunted with small leaves and dropped flowers.
Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.management: No cure. Remove infected plants, control whiteflies, use insect-proof netting and resistant varieties.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.cause: Virus (ToMV); very stable, spread on hands, tools and seed.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic mottling, distorted leaves, stunted growth.
Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.management: No cure. Remove infected plants, disinfect tools and hands, use resistant varieties and certified seed.

Tomato___healthy.management: No disease detected. Keep monitoring the plant: check both leaf sides weekly, water at the base, and remove fallen debris.
